realMachineTests.transcript: keyed-scheduler.ts extracted (197 lines, per-run closure state, explicit cancellation policy) and full-suite-runner.ts imports it. Independently reproduced the real-machine claim behind this item myself: built packages/main, then ran npm test fresh in this worktree and observed exit 0 with "full-suite: 49/49 passed in 363.2s; retries=0; jobs=2" -- this is the actual npm test entrypoint that now runs on the extracted core scheduler, not a paraphrase of the story's own evidence. The happy-path checklist intent (CHK-001:happy:0) carries a waiver instead of a mechanical receipt because its pin selector is the literal string "full-suite: 47/47 passed" from an earlier 47-member suite; the suite is now 49 members so that exact string can never occur again. I confirmed independently that no lightweight repair path exists: checklist.ts enforces verificationIntentProtectedPhases = ['DEV','REVIEW','TEST','DONE'], refusing any verificationIntent edit once a story leaves PLAN, and the only repair-flavoured command in the CLI (verification_intent_repair) is documented and coded as a different thing entirely -- back-filling MISSING intent lanes from existing passing evidence, not rewriting an existing intent's selector text. The waiver's premise is therefore accurate, not a convenience.

packages/main/tests/validate-resource-claims.test.mjs is new (327 lines, 35 assert/VI-OK/throw sites), read directly from the diff and confirmed non-trivial. It drives the real resolveValidationCommandResources/runScheduled path and asserts: an undeclared command resolves to a single exclusive claim and never overlaps any other command (including declared ones in the same 4-command plan at jobs=4); two commands with disjoint declared claims are admitted concurrently; and an unrecognised resource class is rejected both at plan-resolution time and when parsing lattice.config.json. Registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands, so it runs on every future validate invocation, not just once.

packages/main/tests/validate-plan-scheduling.test.mjs is new (230 lines, 60 assert/VI-OK/throw sites), read directly from the diff. It imports the BUILT dist/core/validation-executor.js and drives real executeValidationPlan with real spawned node children, asserting commands[]/details[] stay in plan order even when completion order is reversed, a failing command does not cancel the rest (run-all policy), an exceeded deadline still throws rather than returning a partial pass, and an aborted abortSignal reaches every concurrently running command. Registered in validate.commands.

packages/main/src/tasks/validate-parallel-equivalence-smoke.ts is new (376 lines) and registered in validate.commands as npm run test:validate-parallel-equivalence, so it is gate-enforced on every validate run, not just a one-off. On a synthetic 6-command fixture it measures the SAME plan at jobs=1 and jobs=4 in one process and prints "validate scheduler: jobs=1 commands=6 declared=5 exclusiveByDefault=1" then "parallel validate scheduler: jobs=4 commands=6 declared=5 exclusiveByDefault=1", fails if any per-command outcome differs between modes, and fails if two conflicting claims are observed overlapping. Separately, the REAL 110-command plan speedup (jobs=1=2225.0s vs jobs=4=1474.9s, 1.51x) comes from an explicitly on-demand, non-gate-enforced script (npm run bench:validate-parallel) that is one sample per mode; the story discloses this honestly as one sample against a previously observed ~28% run-to-run spread on this host, rather than presenting it as a precise constant, and summary.json's outcomeDiff states plainly that the measured 1.51x is below the 3.17x the story's background predicted and names why (quorum-submit-smoke alone is ~46% of the parallel makespan). This disclosure is prominent (the dedicated outcomeDiff field), not buried.

Declaration coverage raised from 36 to 97 of 110 commands via lattice.config.json edits, covered by additional cases in validate-resource-claims.test.mjs (same file as CHK-002, gate-registered) asserting the configured plan classifies to 110 commands / 97 declared / 13 exclusive-by-default and that the 10 commands the audit proved unsafe to share remain undeclared barriers. I independently confirmed "validate scheduler: jobs=4 commands=110 declared=97 exclusiveByDefault=13" appears as real captured output in this story's own review-passes.json and test-evidence.json, matching the waiver's restated numbers. CHK-005:happy:0 also carries a permanent waiver for the same structural reason as CHK-001 (pin selector encodes a mutable plan-count prose line, no repair path exists outside a full PLAN reopen); the waiver honestly separates what is proven (declaration coverage, the 10 audited barriers) from what is not (that the extra declarations actually moved wall time -- the only real-plan measurement held declared count constant at 97 on both sides).

closingSelfCheck.summary: Diff touches zero .md documentation files, so docsPromises is correctly empty rather than missing something. I independently reproduced the story's central real-machine claim myself (fresh npm test run in this worktree: full-suite: 49/49 passed in 363.2s, exit 0), confirmed all 13 command-backed checklist evidence rows are bound to the exact merge commit SHA (19ff5225fa1aa3e3482119c148254c8d5f37aa10), and confirmed the two permanent waivers (CHK-001:happy:0, CHK-005:happy:0) are honest: their stated blocker (an immutable pin selector encoding a mutable count, with no repair path) checks out in code -- checklist.ts refuses any verificationIntent edit once a story leaves PLAN, and the CLI's only repair-named command back-fills missing intent lanes, it does not rewrite selector text. The outcomeDiff disclosure (measured 1.51x vs a predicted 3.17x) is prominent and gives a specific, checkable causal explanation rather than hand-waving. One genuine but non-blocking gap: the new operator-facing surface this story adds -- the resources claim field on validate.commands entries and the npm run bench:validate-parallel entry point -- is documented only in inline code comments (validation-types.ts, keyed-scheduler.ts, and an unusually thorough top-of-file docstring in validate-parallel-benchmark.ts) and in summary.json usage text, with no README/CLAUDE.md mention. This is not a broken promise (nothing in a doc claims otherwise) and the repo's README does not document any other validate.commands schema field or npm script either, so this story is not an outlier against an established convention; the fail-closed default also means a future contributor who never finds the comment gets a correct-but-slower barrier rather than a silent correctness bug. Recommend a short CLAUDE.md or decision-doc addendum as low-priority follow-up, not a delivery blocker.
